A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same SEVAL research. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables and figures support comparison despite retitling and substantial reorganization.

before.justification: V2 reports original SEVAL benchmark experiments, ablations and pseudo-label analyses, including Small-ImageNet-127 results in Appendix B.

after.justification: V3 retains these original experiments and adds comparator results, test-prior adaptation experiments and expanded sensitivity and diagnostic analyses.

M1.justification: V3 adds test-prior-weighted SEVAL-W/SEVAL-INV variants (Appendix E) and reverses the threshold-optimization condition from alpha_c > t to alpha_c < t. Its offset objective changes from sample-averaged Eq. 6 in v2 to class-balanced Eq. 7, although v3 Algorithm 2 still retains the unweighted objective. These are extensions and formulation corrections within SEVAL; implementation changes behind retained results are not established.

E1.justification: All five benchmark datasets are retained; Small-ImageNet-127 already appeared in v2 Appendix B.2. V3 Appendix E adds hypothetical non-uniform test-class-prior scenarios through frequency-weighted and inverse-frequency-weighted CIFAR10-LT evaluation.

E2.justification: V3 Table 2 adds SimPro and MetaExpert across the six existing CIFAR/STL settings while retaining previous comparators. Appendix G.1 documents a SimPro adaptation using FixMatch-style hard pseudo-labels in several low-label settings.

E3.justification: Appendix E introduces weighted and inverse-weighted accuracy evaluations with models optimized for matching test priors, and Appendix F.1 extends the t-sensitivity settings. Established training budgets and the existing hyperparameter table remain unchanged. Conflicting new holdout counts do not establish that the existing splits actually changed.

E4.justification: V3 adds test-prior mismatch/adaptation analysis (Table 7), extends Gain and Correctness diagnostics to CIFAR100-LT (Figures 4-5), and expands threshold sensitivity checks (Table 8). Together these substantially extend the evidence on applicability and pseudo-label quality; the earlier component ablations and low-label stress tests are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report three random seeds and retain the same variance-reporting practice. V3 newly specifies that seeds control dataset splitting and initialization; it does not report increased run counts or new significance-testing procedures.

E6.justification: Retained scores in Tables 2-6 and the Small-ImageNet-127 comparison are unchanged. V3 adds SimPro/MetaExpert scores, expanded diagnostic and sensitivity results, and test-prior adaptation results: Table 7 reports 92.5 for SEVAL-W under Weighted AVG and 86.0 for SEVAL-INV under Inverse Weighted AVG. These are new results under their respective evaluations, not gains over the earlier benchmark scores.

T1.justification: V3 adds the constrained equal-precision threshold derivation (Remark 3, Eqs. 8-13), a Neyman-Pearson connection (Appendix D), non-uniform-prior mathematics (Appendix E), and an explicit corollary proof. Proposition 1's proof also gains a no-covariate-shift assertion. The Rademacher-bound theorem and its proof were already present in v2 and are renumbered.

C1.justification: V3 strengthens the stated thresholding contribution from efficient strategies to optimal, theoretically grounded THA, tied to the new equal-precision argument. The principal claims about SEVAL's benchmark competitiveness and compatibility with other SSL frameworks remain.

C2.justification: V3 adds qualifications about fixed experimental hyperparameters and possible degradation with out-of-distribution unlabeled samples (Section 5.5.1 and Appendix F.1). It also states a curriculum-transfer hypothesis and discusses how target test priors affect adjustment benefits (Appendix E).

D1.justification: V3 adds SimPro implementation details, parameter-selection guidance, ImageNet-127's stated ten held-out samples per class, and a held-out-count table. The code URL and existing hyperparameter table are unchanged. Some new counts are inconsistent: Table 12 lists 500 held-out head-class samples for CIFAR10-LT with n1=500, whereas the text specifies k=n/2.

R1.justification: Related work substantially expands to include SimPro, ProCo, MetaExpert, CPG, CoLA and recent SSL applications, alongside the new Neyman-Pearson positioning. V3 develops the statistical-versus-heuristic comparison of PLR/THA more fully and introduces a separate hybrid-solutions subsection.

P1.justification: V3 extensively rewrites the introduction, related work and method explanations. It restructures Section 4, moves existing algorithms to Appendix B and existing threshold-weighting/grouping material into the main text, adds a notation glossary, and reorganizes the appendices. The title and front matter also change.

P2.justification: V3 adds the PLR failure-case diagram, test-prior and held-out-count tables, and glossary display; redraws the overview; and reorganizes and expands v2 Figure 3 into v3 Figures 4-5. Expanded table structures and the TMLR page design substantially alter presentation, while several other figures are retained and renumbered.

improvement.justification: V3 adds useful newer baselines, test-prior experiments and broader sensitivity evidence, and corrects the thresholding condition. However, the new class-balanced objective conflicts with Algorithm 2, and Table 12's held-out counts conflict with the half-split rule. Its stronger equal-precision optimality claims also rely on an approximate derivation. These empirical and explanatory gains coexist with unresolved method-specification and theoretical-support problems, making the net quality change uncertain.
